en: The Ritual for Accomplishment at All Times and in All Places of the Great Blissful Amoghasiddhi Vajrasattva from the *Vajraśekhara Samantabhadrayoga Mahātantrarāja Sūtra*
I prostrate and pay homage to the Great Secret, born from Vajradhara, whose mantra brings easy accomplishment.

I shall now explain the ritual for recitation; there are preliminary secret words that must first be attended to, through which one generates the resolve to bring all beings to the limit of benefit and happiness.
Without exception for the realm of sentient beings, one should recite this mantra of the accomplishment of nature according to one's inclination;
one should generate the bodhicitta as described above, which is called the "vow-bodhicitta."
By merely reciting the secret mantra and generating the bodhicitta,
all obstacles are completely eliminated; one attains all forms of joy and delight,
remains unimpeded by any māras, and becomes equal to the Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Receiving the offerings of all worlds, he further contemplates all phenomena and penetrates directly to the fundamental mind; perfectly white like the full moon,
with five peaks of pure vajra, he stands leaping upon the face of a lunar disc.
Then, the wisdom-vajra is transformed into the body of the Bhagavān Vajrasattva;
his form and attire are like the bright moon,
he sits upon a white lotus pedestal, and his crown is adorned by the five buddhas.
Fully adorned with ornaments and regalia, with a blazing red light on the back,
one dwells within a moon disc; furthermore,
the heart-moon disc is adorned with five vajras— thus one visualizes one's own body.
With two vajra-fists, the left placed on the hip and the right at the heart is called the Vajrasattva pride-mudrā;
with the *hūṃkāra* wisdom-posture pressing down upon the thighs, it is called the Samantabhadra full-lotus posture.
Furthermore, one should bind the mudrā of the wondrous and delightful samaya;
the collection of all perfections should be bound. Taking power and wisdom as its root, with the form of dhyāna, one enters that gate;
moving slowly and with stability, one should apply pressure.
Recite the *sūtra* mantra: *Svāhā siddhaṃ*.
By means of this mudrā and secret mantra, place the noble mudrā upon one's own body at the heart, forehead, throat, and crown; then form the *samādhi-muṣṭi*.
Entering into the center with both meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*), advance and place the strength [of the hands] upon the back.
Recite *oṃ vajra-muṣṭi vaṃ* and form two *karmamudrās*. Then recite *sarvasiddhi*.
Again, arrange the seal of the preceding curtain. Recite the secret mantra of the heart of Mahāsukha-vajra:
HŪṂ KĀRA. Next, join the vajra palms with the earth-touching and boon-granting fingers joined like a lotus; place the forefinger on the first joint.
Placing [the syllable] on the right side of the crown of the head forms the five-buddha crown;
the secret mantra for this shall now be explained.
One should recite "Oṃ Bukkhaṃ" for Vairocana at the crown, and for Akṣobhya at the hairline.
When reciting "Vajra-sattva," one accomplishes the Secret Mantra Crown;
to the right is Ratnasambhava Buddha, also called "Vajra-ratna," which accomplishes the *daśa* (ten); thereafter is Amitāyus Buddha.
Furthermore, by reciting Vajra-dharma, one accomplishes the secret mantra of the Crown;
by reciting Amogha, one accomplishes the secret mantra of the Buddha;
and with Vajra-karma, one forms the supreme mudrā that divides the body of the Buddha.
Form two vajra-fists; crossing the arms at the level of the forehead, extend the fists to the temples.
Interlace the forearms at the joints and bind them three times with the vajra-garland;
then separate the hands to rest beside the two ears.
From *dāna* and *prajñā*, passing through *vikiraṇa*, one is imbued with the grace of hanging silk ribbons;
reciting *vajra-maṇḍala vaṃ*, by means of these mudrās and so forth,
one receives the full ordination and empowerment.
For the sake of explaining the Noble Assembly, clap the hands together three times with the palms slightly apart while reciting *vajradṛk*.
By clapping the vajra-palms according to the secret syllables *sya huṃ*,
one swiftly accomplishes the essence of the Sattva.
Next, one should establish them all: the Great Blissful One is surrounded by his retinue of sixteen deities.
In front of him, at the position of the eyes, are two hands holding a bow and arrow; his form and raiment are the color of a red lotus.
With two vajra-fists, draw the bow according to the ritual for shooting;
recite "Jvalavajra" and the mantra "Iriṣṭiśaya kīmatā," and then "Kīlīkila" on the right.
With arms crossed in the vajra-fist, the right hand internally grasps a vajra in the shape of a moon; with lotus-eyes,
recite *HŪṂ VAJRA KĪLI KĪLE HŪṂ*, and thereafter further hold a banner and a pennant.
Maṅgala is the foremost; the Fist of Wisdom with arm raised at the elbow, the power of the fixed fist, and the water of wisdom;
his form and eyes are like the blue lotus, Vaṃ Vāyulini; Samara-raṭa.
Having recited this secret mantra, place both fists at the sides of the waist and slightly lower the head to the left;
then recite the secret mantra *krodhavajrakāminī tvaṃ*.
The Vajrapaṭa resides on the left; the yellow Lotus-body of the Mind is in the front right corner during the spring. With both hands he holds a lotus-dish-shaped vessel;
his garment is white like a lotus; with two fists raised upward, he makes the scattering gesture.
Name-flowers fill the realm of space; one should recite *oṃ madhuvajra kuṃ*.
Thereafter, at the right corner, one should hold the incense burner and offer burning incense; the color of the body is like hanging clouds.
Covering the two [hands] and pressing them downward, the fragrant clouds pervade with a pervasive scent.
Recite that secret mantra: Oṃ Vajra-mañju-yulu yulu. Thereafter, at the left corner, it is autumn.
Holding a red lamp, with meditative concentration and wisdom joined together,
the vajra-lamp is extended all around; then recite *Oṃ śara-vā-dhā-ri-aṅku*,
sprinkling and wiping it upon one's own chest.
This constitutes the mudrā of the ointment fragrance (*vilepana*). Recite:
*Oṃ vajraśīle hūṃ hūṃ*. Holding the bowl of ointment fragrance, she abides in the front left corner;
her body is white, her lotus garment is yellow.
In the outer maṇḍala, one should establish flowers in the four corners;
the directions are named *hāsya* (laughter). Placing two fists inverted over the heart, one should rotate [the hands] while reciting *he ratī vajravailā*.
Sittirattala, raising the palms and pointing toward the sides of the mouth, recite *hīrati* with a smile; *vajra-hāse hā hā karaya*.
This is called "Smiling Abiding Beyond the Clouds."
Autumn Outer Vajra Song: The fist of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-muṣṭi*) slightly bends the power of the *vīṇā*;
The arm is drawn back like a *vīṇā*, and the fist of wisdom (*prajñā-muṣṭi*) is likewise advanced;
Between the arms of meditative concentration and wisdom, [the two fists meet].
Singing *gīta*, *vajragīte gīte*—the secret mantra is thus accomplished.
Performing the wheel dance with the various *mudrās*, one releases the fists and then forms them again;
turning the left and right cheeks upward.
Scattering from the vajra-palms, recite *heṣṭe vajra-īḍiṭi*.
At the outer corners where the dancing has ceased, say *vepa vepa*. These are the four offerings.

Both possess golden-colored bodies; with the hands joined in the *tāṇa-hṛdaya* (charity-wisdom) gesture, they extend their arms in the *pāramitā* (perfection) pose. The first fingers of the right hands are bent like hooks;
one should recite *vākye*. This is the *kūṭa-śakti* (peak-power) secret mantra.
Holding the hook, protect the eastern gate;
then, with the power of advancement, form a loop like a ring to create a lasso.
Furthermore, recite the secret mantra *vajrapāśe hūṃ* while grasping the lasso to guard the southern gate.
With the power of progress, bind the joints firmly;
stepping across, one should recite the mantra *vajra-śaṅkari vaṃ*.
Having performed this secret speech, step across and dwell at the rear gate, without altering the previous mudrā-form.
When the mind slightly wavers, the name "Vajraghaṇṭā" (Vajra Bell) resounds.
Having recited the secret mantra *vajraghaṇṭi*, hold the ghaṇṭā and protect the left gate;
the form and color of the Honored One of the Four Means of Attraction [is as follows].
One should apply four subtle particles of clay within; as above, these sixteen honored ones are thus perfected.
They are wondrously peaceful and reside as guests; beautiful and radiant, they possess every graceful posture.
Seated upon lotuses in the full-lotus position (paryaṅka), they all abide supported by lunar discs.
Adorned with all manner of ornaments, he uses them to grace his body;
he wears the crowns of the five Buddhas, and his robes, colored like lotuses according to his own hue, delight the eye. Behold him as he holds the vajra.
Having thus established it, one completes the maṇḍala;
within it, in the shape of a wheel, it is adorned with eight pillars.
Between the supreme vajra pillars, it is embellished with moon discs.
That outer maṇḍala should have four sides and four gates;
the four outer gates correspond [to the inner ones].
The doorways are joined and adorned with vajra-jewels; such are the corners of the maṇḍala.
Adorned for half a month, with necklaces, bells,
and silk banners suspended everywhere, a gentle breeze stirred them,
producing harmonious and elegant sounds that resonated throughout the surrounding vajra-realm.
With space as the palace, one should contemplate with such precision that the maṇḍala resides within it;
established by the mind at all times and in all directions, one’s own body becomes the deity.
With such offerings as these, one should circumambulate and present one's own body;
whether walking or standing, one should always follow [the deity].
Regarding all forms that are seen, one should contemplate them all as empty, and further reflect upon the body of the tutelary deity.
Recite: Oṃ kalu mu kha sarvadharmān āmṛśanupamān svāhā.
Or, using the secret words or grass, recite the syllable Oṃ and contemplate with self-concentration.
Scented ointments, lamps, and incense; flower garlands, food, drink, clothing, precious banners, and canopies; fans, fly-whisks, pennants, and bells;
manifesting songs, dances, and magnificent palaces throughout the entirety of the realm of space.
I now transform all these supreme offerings for the enjoyment of the assembly of noble ones; then, recite the four kings of praises,
the arrow, the embrace, the banner, and the canopy mudrās, while chanting the Vajra-Desire mantra.
*Sarvanulokasu-khasattvam anupraviśa tvaṃ vajrasattvaparamasaukhyam* (Enter into all worlds, O you who are the essence of the sky;
enter into me, O Vajrasattva, the supreme bliss).
Bhavaṃ mahā-sukha-īśvara-yajña-dhvaja | Pratipanna-siddhi-cakra-guṇa-praṇata-mān ||
By means of this vajra song, great bliss follows after delight,
and with firm joy as its essence, all attain the fulfillment of their wishes through words of sublime rapture;
one should recite the syllable *A* according to one's capacity.
All phenomena are fundamentally unarisen; one should know that such is their meaning.
The essence of great bliss is not empty. Constantly recite the *hūṃkāra* and the Dharma-seal of Vajragarbha, and place the secret mantra according to your will.
HŪṂ KĀRA, or otherwise, as one recites, blazing flames emerge from every pore,
like a pure crystal or the white moonlight appearing in the sun; [this is] the Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind.
All should perform this contemplation with truth:
the recitation of the vajra speech that accomplishes all teachings; reciting without sound by joining the lips and teeth while slightly moving the tongue—practice in this manner.
Until a full month has passed, or two, or six months, the signs that were contemplated will all appear.
Having personally attained the peaceful body of a *sattva*, one stands before the assembly of noble ones; there, with *oṃ kāru*, one makes offerings.
Furthermore, offer the eight offerings: Sing the four praises with the vajra *vaṃ* joined together;
With the fingers of patience and aspiration like a banner, recite *Oṃ kṛto va-sarva-sattvān*.
NATĀYATHA NU | GA-SA-SVA-THI-MUN-BUDHA-VISHAYAN | PUNA-RĀGA-MANA-SHTO-OM VAJRA-SATTVA-MUKHA ||

Having recited this secret mantra, one should form the mudrā at the crown of the head and release it with the fists opened to dismiss the assembly of noble beings. As they flow out from the crown of the head,
if one wishes to do so at all times, one should direct the mind according to this ritual procedure.
Seeing all forms and so forth, one should imagine them as offerings to the *iṣṭadevatā* (personal deity).
Contemplating that the form of one's own body is empty, and thinking,
"This is my own *iṣṭadevatā*," is called the "eye of resolute conviction" (*adhimukti-cakṣus*).
Whatever various forms are perceived, one should contemplate them all as empty;
furthermore, contemplate the body of Vajrasattva. Know that these, together with the Honored One, are all fundamentally empty, and thus become one single essence.
Abiding in such yoga, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
one should recite the mantra while visualizing the light. Upon completing one hundred thousand recitations,
one should remain awake throughout the night without sleep, continuing the recitation until dawn.
Furthermore, at all times, using the aforementioned exquisite and pleasing samaya and garland,
recite each respective root mantra so that one’s own body becomes the deity;
then, settle the mind in the yoga of mental focus.

Thereafter, one should perform the recitation within the *maṇḍala* during four sessions until a total of one hundred thousand recitations are completed; furthermore, during the final watch of the night,
one should remain awake as before and continue the recitation until dawn.
Before long, one shall achieve the body of the deity and the body of the Buddha;
even this will not be difficult to attain, let alone the various *siddhis*.
The excellent Ācārya Śubhagupta has compiled these subtle and wondrous meanings.
I have briefly expounded this great sūtra, compiling its most profound and secret intent.
Those who do not enter the maṇḍala yet presume to employ these teachings will incur the defilement of sin;
as described in all the various scriptures, such an act constitutes a grave transgression that creates a heavy karmic obstruction.
There is nothing that can extinguish it; the great seal of Vajrasattva, when bound, can extinguish everything.
One who cultivates this samādhi accomplishes all dharmas through the power of the mind; this is not taught in any other instruction.
All are accomplished according to one's will; as soon as the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) is bound, the Tathāgatas all pay homage.
The holder of the secret mantra is the supreme sovereign of all Buddhas through the majestic power of the Great Seal.
Tranquil, supreme, and peerless, one need not perform various ritual procedures;
by binding only the single great mudrā, no one can create obstacles,
and one swiftly attains accomplishment while guarding the original samaya.
Without causing suffering to body or mind, may they experience bliss and attain accomplishment;
may all sentient beings, through faith and acceptance,
enter this Dharma and swiftly achieve the state of Vajrasattva.
The Universal Illumination, Firm Essence, and the Various Bodies Accordant with Vows.

From the *Samantabhadra-yoga-sūtra*, the *Sādhana-vidhi of Mahāsukha-vajrasattva*. On the fourteenth day of the eighth month in the third year of the Dali era, the monk Yuanli of Qinglong Monastery in the Western Capital transcribed this record of the Sanskrit and Chinese characters. On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month in the first year of the Yingde era, at the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), it was copied from the Tang edition held in the Tiantangyuan at the Guilin Chamber. This Tang edition of the *Qianshou-yigui* was recorded by Tie’er Liang.
